title: RenewKit: renewals, payments and a public member register for small trade associations
source: Top 50 research (Nov 2026): reframed from ideas dropped from the Top 25 report, plus new web research
summary: Small trade associations and professional bodies spend weeks every year chasing renewals by email and spreadsheet. RenewKit sends renewal reminders with payment links, keeps the public "find a member" register up to date automatically, and wins back lapsed members, without moving the association to a big membership system.
hook: "Renewal season is three months of me sending the same email to 600 members and checking bank statements by hand."
story:
**Karin is the only staff member of a national association of 640 certified installers.** Members pay **€350 a year** and, in return, appear in the association's public "find a certified installer" list, which brings them customers. Renewals run from a spreadsheet, a bank account and a mail-merge.

Every spring Karin spends about **three months** chasing late payers, updating the website list by hand, and answering "did you get my payment?" emails. Some members who never paid still appear on the website; some who paid are missing. A full membership system like Wild Apricot would mean moving the website and everything else, and its prices keep rising. She wants renewals and the register to run themselves.
whyNow: Membership software prices are rising and ownership is consolidating (Wild Apricot is now part of Momentive Software), which pushes small bodies to look for lighter options. Payment links and AI-written reminders make a "renewals only" tool simple to build.
evidence: Wild Apricot's entry plan is reported at $66/month for 100 contacts, up from $60 in April 2026; users report earlier price rises of 20% (2021) and 25% (2023) [CostBench / Hackceleration]
Momentive Software acquired Personify, Wild Apricot's owner, on 6 January 2026 (reported by a competitor) [Raklet]
In the Top 25 research, association renewals scored 44/70 at best, with crowded incumbents and volunteer buyers who churn when officers change [Top 25 research notes]
Many small software categories for clubs and schools start around $15/month, which shows low willingness to pay at the bottom of the market [TutorBird via Top 25 report]

whyReal.title: Renewal season is real work
whyReal.text: Small associations with one staff member or volunteers spend weeks chasing payments every year.

whyReal.title: The register is the strongest hook
whyReal.text: For trade bodies, being listed as a member brings customers. Linking the public list to payment makes members pay on time.

whyReal.title: No migration needed
whyReal.text: RenewKit plugs into the existing website and spreadsheet instead of replacing everything, which lowers the fear of switching.

whyReal.title: Honest weakness
whyReal.text: Buyers are price-sensitive and often volunteers; this is a modest business, not a big one.

whoPays.label: Customer
whoPays.text: Trade associations, professional bodies and chambers with 100–3,000 business or professional members and 0–3 staff.

whoPays.label: Buyer
whoPays.text: The executive director, secretary or treasurer.

whoPays.label: Start market
whoPays.text: UK, Ireland, Nordics and other English-speaking associations found through public directories.

solution.title: Import members
solution.text: upload the member spreadsheet; set membership types, prices and renewal dates.

solution.title: Automatic renewals
solution.text: reminders with a personal payment link (card, SEPA, invoice) go out before and after the due date; AI writes friendly reminder texts.

solution.title: Live member register
solution.text: an embeddable "find a member" list for the website that shows only paid-up members, with their certificates and regions.

solution.title: Lapsed-member win-back
solution.text: members who do not renew get a short sequence and the association sees revenue at risk.

solution.title: Self-service
solution.text: members update their details and download receipts and membership certificates.

must: Member import from CSV / Google Sheets
Stripe payment links and invoice option

timeline.what: Jonatan emails 300 small associations from public directories offering a free "renewal audit" (lapsed members, revenue at risk). Goal: 10 calls, 3 pilots.
Import, membership types, payment links, reminders.
Public register widget, dashboard, self-service, billing.
Run one real renewal season with pilots; measure on-time payment rate.

risks.answer: Target trade bodies with paid certifications and public registers, where members pay €200+ a year.
Annual plans, and make RenewKit hold the member history so a new treasurer inherits it.
Stay narrow: renewals and register only; integrate with what they have.

questions: How do members renew today, and who chases late payers?
What share of members did not renew last year?
Do members get listed publicly? How do you keep that list up to date?
What tools do you use and what do they cost?
Would you pay €49–89 a month if renewals and the register ran themselves?
